morphemes.label: linking vowel (low stem: a, not o)

explain: Order is always stem → (linking vowel) → number/possessive → case. ház is a back stem, so every two-form suffix takes its back form.
Two-form suffix: back stem → -ban. The case attaches straight to the base, no linking vowel.
Two-form suffix: front stem → -ben.

morphemes.label: inessive — in (front form; two-form suffixes have no separate rounded form)

explain: Front-rounded stems take the same -ben as plain front stems: two-form suffixes only distinguish back vs front.
Three-form suffix after a consonant: back stem → -on.
Three-form suffix: front unrounded stem → -en.
Three-form suffix: last vowel ö → -ön. Only three-form suffixes have this rounded variant.

morphemes.label: allative — to, up to (back form of -hoz/-hez/-höz)

explain: Three-form suffix: back stem → -hoz. Attaches directly to the base.

morphemes.label: allative — to, up to (front unrounded form of -hoz/-hez/-höz)

explain: Three-form suffix: front unrounded stem → -hez.

morphemes.label: allative — to, up to (front rounded form of -hoz/-hez/-höz)

explain: Three-form suffix: last vowel ö → -höz.
Movement into → -ba/-be. Back stem → -ba.

morphemes.label: restaurant (front-vowel stem; full form, the fleeting e stays before a case suffix)

explain: Case suffixes attach to the full stem étterem-; the fleeting vowel drops only before linking-vowel suffixes (éttermet, éttermek).

morphemes.label: car (back-vowel stem, ends in a long vowel — no lengthening needed)

explain: Movement onto → -ra/-re. Back stem → -ra.

morphemes.label: Budapest — mixed-vowel name that behaves as a FRONT stem (exception)
delative — off / from the surface of; also 'about' (front form of -ról/-ről)

explain: Budapest takes front suffixes (Budapesten, Budapestre, Budapestről) even though it has back vowels — learn it as an exception.

morphemes.label: adessive — at, by, near (back form of -nál/-nél)

explain: Being near/at someone or something → -nál/-nél. Back stem → -nál.

morphemes.label: ablative — from (away from near) (back form of -tól/-től)

explain: Movement away from someone/something → -tól/-től. Back stem → -tól.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before plural -k (low stem: a, not o)

explain: Plural -k needs a linking vowel after a consonant; ház is a low stem, so a. Case comes last.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before plural -k (front stem: e)

explain: Front stem: linking vowel e, suffix -ben.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before plural -k — könyv takes e, not ö

explain: The plural linking vowel is a lexical property: könyv → könyvek (not *könyvök), unlike sör → sörök.

morphemes.label: plural — no linking vowel after a vowel
superessive — on (back form of -on/-en/-ön, after the consonant k)

explain: Vowel-final stems add -k directly. After plural -k the superessive needs its full form -on.
After z the accusative -t needs a linking vowel; ház is a low stem, so a.

morphemes.label: accusative — direct object; -t attaches directly after l (also after r, n, ny, s, sz, z, zs, j)

explain: Stems ending in l, r, n, ny, s, sz, z, zs, j usually take -t with no linking vowel: asztalt, tanárt, várost.
After k the accusative needs a linking vowel; front stem → e.

morphemes.label: dog — final a lengthens to á before a suffix
accusative — direct object (-t directly after a vowel)

explain: Vowel-final stems take -t directly; a final short a/e lengthens first (kutya → kutyát).

morphemes.label: linking vowel before the possessive (low stem: a)

explain: Possessive before case: ház-a-m-ban. Same linking vowel as the plural (házak, házam).

morphemes.label: 3SG possessor -je (kert takes j); its final e lengthens to é before the case

explain: kertje + ben → kertjében: the possessive's final e lengthens before a case suffix.

morphemes.label: 1PL possessor — our (-nk after a vowel; -unk/-ünk after a consonant)
instrumental -val: v assimilates to the final k (autónk + val → autónkkal)

explain: After a vowel the 1PL possessive is just -nk. -val then assimilates to the k: autónkkal.

morphemes.label: 3SG possessor -ja (barát takes j); its final a lengthens to á before the case

explain: barátja + tól → barátjától: lengthening of the possessive's final a before the case suffix.

morphemes.label: j + linking vowel e before plural-possessed -i (kert is a j-stem: kertje, kertjeim)

explain: Stems with 3SG -je usually keep the j in the plural possessed: kertje → kertjei → kertjeim → kertjeimben.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before plural-possessed -i — no j here although 3SG is barátja

explain: barát takes j in barátja but not in the plural possessed: barátaim, barátai, barátaink.

morphemes.label: linking vowel e before plural-possessed -i (always a/e here, never ö)

explain: Plural possessed: könyv-e-i-d; -ról/-ről after a noun often means 'about'.

morphemes.label: hand — kéz shortens to kez- before a linking-vowel suffix

explain: Vowel-shortening stem: kéz → kezet, kezek, kezem; but kézben, kézzel keep the long vowel.

morphemes.label: horse — ló becomes lov- before linking-vowel suffixes
linking vowel before -t (lov- is a low stem: a)

explain: v-stem: ló → lovat, lovak, lovam, lovon; but lóban, lóval.

morphemes.label: bird — madár shortens to madar- before a linking-vowel suffix
linking vowel before plural -k (low stem: a)

explain: Vowel-shortening stem: madár → madarak, madarat, madaram; but madárban, madárral.

morphemes.label: fire — tűz shortens to tüz- before a linking-vowel suffix
linking vowel before -t (e, even for this ü-stem)

explain: Vowel-shortening stem: tűz → tüzet, tüzek, tüzem; but tűzben, tűzzel.

morphemes.label: road — út shortens to ut- before a linking-vowel suffix

explain: Vowel-shortening stem: út → utat, utak, utam; but úton, útja, úttal.

morphemes.label: stone — kő becomes köv- before linking-vowel suffixes

explain: v-stem: kő → kövek, követ, kövem, kövön; but kőben, kővel.

morphemes.label: instrumental -val: v assimilates to the final consonant (ház + val → házzal)

explain: -val/-vel after a consonant: the v becomes a copy of that consonant.

morphemes.label: instrumental -vel: v assimilates to the final t (kert + vel → kerttel)

explain: Front stem → -vel; after t the v becomes t: kerttel.

morphemes.label: bus — busz; the final digraph sz is doubled as ssz, so the second s belongs with the suffix in this split
instrumental -val: v assimilates to sz; a doubled digraph is written by doubling only its first letter (sz → ssz)

explain: busz + val → busszal. Doubled digraphs double only the first letter: ssz, ggy, ccs, nny.

morphemes.label: mountain — hegy; the final digraph gy is doubled as ggy, so the y belongs with the suffix in this split
instrumental -vel: v assimilates to gy; the doubled digraph is spelled ggy

explain: hegy + vel → heggyel. Same rule as busszal: gy → ggy.

morphemes.label: dog — final a lengthens to á before a suffix

explain: kutya + ban → kutyában: a final short a lengthens before every suffix.

morphemes.label: dog — final a lengthens to á before a suffix
plural — no linking vowel after a vowel

explain: Vowel-final stem: plural is just -k, with the final a lengthened: kutyák.

morphemes.label: apple — final a lengthens to á before a suffix
accusative — direct object (-t directly after a vowel)

explain: alma + t → almát: lengthening, then -t directly.
Dative -nak/-nek is a two-form suffix: back stem → -nak.
Front stem → -nek.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before plural -k — sör takes ö (three-form linking vowel o/e/ö)

explain: The plural linking vowel can be o/e/ö by harmony: sörök, but könyvek — it is lexical, learn it with the noun.
Three-form linking vowel: gyümölcsöt, gyümölcsök, gyümölcsöm.

morphemes.label: passport — út+levél; levél shortens to level- before a linking-vowel suffix
linking vowel before -t (harmony follows the last member levél: front, e)

explain: Compounds follow their last member: útlevél behaves like levél → útlevelet, útlevelek, útlevelem; útlevélben, útlevéllel.

morphemes.label: 3SG possessor -ja (család takes j); its final a lengthens to á before the case
instrumental — with (-val unchanged after a vowel)

explain: After a vowel -val/-vel does not assimilate: családjá + val → családjával.

morphemes.label: consulate (back stem: o, u, á, u)
superessive — on/at (back form of -on/-en/-ön); used for institutions you are 'at'

explain: Many institutions and events take the surface case: a konzulátuson, a pályaudvaron, az egyetemen.

morphemes.label: school — final a lengthens to á before a suffix

explain: iskola + ba → iskolába: lengthening, then the back two-form suffix.

morphemes.label: grandmother — final a lengthens to á before a suffix
1SG possessor — my (no linking vowel after a vowel)

explain: Vowel-final stem: possessive -m attaches directly after lengthening; then the case: nagymamámnak.

morphemes.label: 1PL possessor — our (-unk after a consonant, back form of -unk/-ünk)

explain: After a consonant the 1PL possessive is -unk/-ünk by harmony: lakásunk, kertünk.
Plural possessed: gyerek-e-i-nk. Compare the plain plural gyerekek.

morphemes.label: restaurant — étterem drops its last e (fleeting vowel) before a linking-vowel suffix
linking vowel before plural -k (front stem: e)

explain: Fleeting-vowel stem: étterem → éttermek, éttermet, éttermem; but étteremben, étteremmel.

morphemes.label: mirror (front-rounded stem; the full form stays before a case suffix)

explain: Fleeting-vowel stem tükör: tükörben, tükörrel keep the ö; tükröt, tükrök, tükröm drop it.

morphemes.label: plural — no linking vowel after a vowel

explain: Plural, then case: szülő-k-től.

morphemes.label: linking vowel before the possessive (front stem: e)
instrumental -vel: v assimilates to the final m of the possessive (testvérem + vel → testvéremmel)

explain: Assimilation applies to whatever consonant ends the word, including a possessive: testvéremmel, barátommal.

morphemes.label: accusative — direct object; -t attaches directly after z

explain: After z, s, sz, l, r, n, ny, j the accusative usually needs no linking vowel: pénzt, várost, embert.

morphemes.label: week — hét shortens to het- before a linking-vowel suffix
linking vowel before plural -k (front stem: e)

explain: Vowel-shortening stem: hét → hetek, hetet, hete; but héten, héttel.

morphemes.label: summer (back stem; the long á stays before a case suffix)
superessive — on; with seasons means 'in' (back form of -on/-en/-ön)

explain: Summer and winter take the surface case: nyáron, télen (but tavasszal, ősszel). The stem shortens only before linking-vowel suffixes (nyarak).
